newsitem.title: USA: U.S SEES GOOD PROSPECTS FOR RICE SALES TO HONDURAS.
newsitem.headline: U.S SEES GOOD PROSPECTS FOR RICE SALES TO HONDURAS.

text.p: Prospects are good for renewed U.S. rough rice sales to Honduras nearly a year after trade was blocked, the U.S. Agriculture Department attache in Guatemala said.
In an August 5 report released Wednesday, the attache estimated that Honduras needs to import 29,000 tonnes, milled equivalent, of rough rice in 1997-98 because of low stocks.
Honduras blocked shipments of U.S. rice in September 1996 when it began requiring proof that the grain came from regions free of the Tilletia Barclayana fungus.
"USDA could not comply... given the fact that this fungus is endemic to all major rice-producing regions of the world, including the United States," the attache noted.
"A recent study conducted by the Honduran Ministry of Agriculture revealed the presence of the fungus in Honduras as well," the attache said.
As such, Honduran authorities have "recently relaxed their policy and are now allowing rough rice to be imported into Honduras," the attache said.
"Although fumigation in the port of export is now required, prospects for U.S. suppliers of rough rice (to Honduras) are looking better than ever," the attache said.
